packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 18 - FIRST READING (unverified image reading)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- No proposed identification or prior reading of this text was in my context. This is a blind reading.
- Beyond the stated rules: (1) I listed the *.jpg files in the packet directory with a shell glob to know the image count (no other directory listed, packet.json not opened); (2) because several fragments are mounted upside down, I made 180-degree rotated copies of images 004-026 in my own scratch directory and read the upside-down fragments from those rotated copies. Line numbers below are counted from the top of the fragment AS READ UPRIGHT, and each line is tied to the packet image(s) it is visible in.
- All 26 images loaded. image-001 and image-014 are reduced overviews (two faces of the same set of six fragments); images 002-013 are tiles of the first face, 015-026 tiles of the second face.
- Visible modern pencil on the fragments (not part of the text): "Stams, STA, Frg. 106-1r ... 6r / 1v ... 6v" piece labels, "aus Urbar IV/42 v. J. 1625" (or similar), and day/month notes such as "14.IX", "4.IX", "1.XI", "2.XI", "6.XI", "7.XI", "8.XI", "11.IX". I record them only to label pieces.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Six parchment strips/pieces cut from (a) leaf/leaves of a single-column (or one column of a multi-column) book, small Gothic textualis/cursiva-influenced bookhand, brown ink, rubrics in red, red (sometimes flourished) 2-line initials, red one-line initials/letters touched in red.
- No running titles, glosses or commentary visible. No underlining. Text is continuous prose punctuated by red rubrics naming occasions/saints and genre labels (an(tiphona), collecta, oratio, historia, lectio numbers "lc ij", "iij", V(ersiculus), R(esponsorium)).
- Tentative interpretation: liturgical office text (rubrics, antiphons, collects, short readings). I do not infer more.
- Pieces as labelled in pencil: 1r/1v (lower right in overview, damaged lower edge); 2r/2v (L-shaped piece, mounted upside down on face 1); 3r/3v (bottom middle, mounted upside down on face 1); 4r/4v (tall strip, top middle); 5r/5v (tall strip, top left); 6r/6v (small piece, bottom left).
- All pieces are cropped on at least one side; most lines are truncated. Overlapping tiles repeat lines; I note overlaps and do not double-count.

SPANS SELECTED
All six pieces, both faces, read as far as the letters go. Unread/uncertain: the topmost cut line of most pieces; the faint offset/erased traces below the text on 6v; parts of 3r lines 8-12 (abraded); the narrow vertical tongue of 2r/2v (only line-ends survive).

Conventions: ( ) expansion; ? after an uncertain reading; [...] text lost at the cut; [illegible] unreadable within the surviving area; (red) rubricated text.

LIMITATIONS
- Every piece is a cut strip; nearly all lines lack beginnings or endings. Column width and original page layout cannot be reconstructed from these crops.
- 3r lines 8-15 and 3v lines 6-11 are abraded; readings there are low confidence.
- Several red rubric words (2r l.5-6, 4r l.21-22, 5r l.22, 5v l.4, 1r l.14, 2v l.6) are uncertain; I give letter-forms with "?".
- Pieces 2 and 3 are mounted upside down on face 1; I read them from rotated copies, so line numbers for those refer to upright orientation.
- 2r/2v vertical tongue preserves only 1-3 letters per line.
- Recto/verso assignment and the order between pieces follow the pencil labels only; I did not verify them.
- Suggest higher-resolution or raking-light views of 3r (lines 8-15), the red rubrics on 2r line 5-6, and the lower half of 6v (faint traces).
